title: The Senate Testimony of William Barr

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访几位商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 您可以实时观看其中一些毫无保留、未经修饰的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在NYTimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, in testimony before the Senate Judiciary Committee, Attorney General William Barr defended his handling of the Mueller report, saying he did not misrepresent its findings.
sentences.zh: 今天，司法部长威廉·巴尔在参议院司法委员会作证时，为他处理穆勒报告的方式进行了辩护，称他没有歪曲报告的调查结果。

sentences.en: My colleague, Nick Fandos, spent the day in the hearing room.
sentences.zh: 我的同事尼克·凡多斯在听证会现场待了一整天。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, May 2nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月2日，星期四。

sentences.en: So the story starts a couple of weeks ago when Bill Barr, after much anticipation, releases the 448-page Mueller report.
sentences.zh: 故事要从几周前说起，当时比尔·巴尔在万众期待中发布了448页的穆勒报告。

sentences.en: At 11 this morning, I'm going to transmit copies of the public version to the chairman and ranking members of the Senate and House Judiciary Committees.
sentences.zh: 今天上午11点，我将把公开版本的副本发送给参议院和众议院司法委员会的主席及资深成员。

sentences.en: Congress is out on recess scattered all over the country and scrambles to figure out what to do next.
sentences.zh: 国会正处于休会期，议员们分散在全国各地，正忙着商讨下一步该怎么做。

sentences.en: But there's one clear expectation, which is whatever happens now, the Justice Department has spoken,
sentences.zh: 但有一个明确的预期，那就是无论现在发生什么，司法部已经表态了，

sentences.en: and it's up to Congress to decide whether or not President Trump will face any sort of consequences for the behavior that was outlined in great detail by Bob Mueller.
sentences.zh: 而特朗普总统是否会因为鲍勃·穆勒详细列出的行为而面临任何后果，则由国会来决定。

sentences.en: That is why I have formally requested that Special Counsel Mueller testify before the House Judiciary Committee as soon as possible.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我已正式要求特别检察官穆勒尽快在众议院司法委员会作证。

sentences.en: So immediately we see Democrats who control the House talk about a number of witnesses that they want to call.
sentences.zh: 所以我们立刻看到控制众议院的民主党人开始讨论他们想要传唤的证人名单。

sentences.en: They issue a subpoena the next day for the full Mueller report and all of the evidence underlying it.
sentences.zh: 第二天，他们就发出传票，要求提供完整的穆勒报告以及所有相关证据。

sentences.en: They want the entire unedited report, not the redacted version sent to them by Attorney General William Barr.
sentences.zh: 他们想要的是未经编辑的完整报告，而不是司法部长威廉·巴尔发给他们的删减版。

sentences.en: Because they want to start recreating and scrutinizing the evidence themselves.
sentences.zh: 因为他们想亲自重新梳理和审查这些证据。

sentences.en: And they very quickly start to call a number of witnesses.
sentences.zh: 而且他们很快就开始传唤多名证人。

sentences.en: There was no collusion with Russia.
sentences.zh: （特朗普：）与俄罗斯没有任何勾结。

sentences.en: Over at the White House, it's a whole other story.
sentences.zh: 而在白宫那边，情况则完全不同。

sentences.en: It was a complete and total exoneration.
sentences.zh: （特朗普：）这是彻底的完全开脱。

sentences.en: And they basically say, this is the end of the investigation.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上说，调查到此结束。

sentences.en: So that makes it a complete and total exoneration.
sentences.zh: （特朗普：）所以这让它成为了一次彻底的完全开脱。

sentences.en: I don't know any other way to look at it.
sentences.zh: 我想不出还有什么别的看法。

sentences.en: We're not going to let you talk to these witnesses.
sentences.zh: 我们不会让你们接触这些证人。

sentences.en: We're not going to voluntarily produce this evidence that you want.
sentences.zh: 我们不会主动提供你们想要的这些证据。

sentences.en: Don McGahn, don't adhere to the subpoena, they say.
sentences.zh: 他们说，唐·麦克加恩，不要理会传票。

sentences.en: I say it's enough.
sentences.zh: （特朗普：）我说够了。

sentences.en: President Trump vows to block all subpoenas, not just for this investigation, but anything that House Democrats are trying to scrutinize of his administration.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统誓言要阻止所有传票，不仅是针对这项调查，还包括众议院民主党人试图对他政府进行的任何审查。

sentences.en: They're basically, you know, trying to put a full stop to this story.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是想给这个故事画上句号。

sentences.en: Get back to infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 回到基础设施建设上来。

sentences.en: Get back to cutting taxes.
sentences.zh: 回到减税上来。

sentences.en: Get back to lowering drug prices.
sentences.zh: 回到降低药价上来。

sentences.en: That's what, really, that's what we should be doing.
sentences.zh: 那才是我们真正应该做的事情。

sentences.en: So now, all of a sudden, Democrats are finding themselves wrestling not just with the obstruction that Bob Mueller detailed in his 448-page report.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，民主党人突然发现自己不仅要应对鲍勃·穆勒在他那448页报告中详述的妨碍司法行为。

sentences.en: They're starting to look around them and say, hey, the president is obstructing us.
sentences.zh: 他们开始环顾四周，心想，嘿，总统正在阻挠我们。

sentences.en: He's obstructing Congress, another branch of government, just as he did the Department of Justice.
sentences.zh: 他正在阻挠国会，即政府的另一个分支，就像他阻挠司法部一样。

sentences.en: And that's serious.
sentences.zh: 这事很严重。

sentences.en: And in the middle of that, the one thing that they've got on the books, the one thing they can count on is that we would have Bill Barr facing 11 Democrats,
sentences.zh: 在此过程中，他们唯一能依靠的、板上钉钉的事情，就是比尔·巴尔将在周三上午10点面对参议院的11名民主党人和

sentences.en: 13 Republicans in the Senate Wednesday morning at 10 a.m.
sentences.zh: 13名共和党人。

sentences.en: The Washington Post is breaking a major story.
sentences.zh: 《华盛顿邮报》正在发布一则重磅新闻。

sentences.en: As we speak, Special Counsel Robert Mueller told Attorney General William Barr that the depiction of his findings failed to capture context, nature, and substance of his probe.
sentences.zh: 就在我们说话的时候，特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒告诉司法部长威廉·巴尔，他对调查结果的描述未能捕捉到其调查的背景、性质和实质。

sentences.en: And then, on Tuesday night, just hours before senators are ready to convene for this hearing, the New York Times and the Washington Post report the existence of a letter.
sentences.zh: 然后，在周二晚上，就在参议员们准备召开听证会的前几个小时，《纽约时报》和《华盛顿邮报》报道了一封信的存在。

sentences.en: Expressed his concerns in a letter to William Barr after the attorney general publicized Mueller's principal conclusions.
sentences.zh: （穆勒在信中）在司法部长公布穆勒的主要结论后，向威廉·巴尔表达了他的担忧。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: This was the four-page letter that Bill Barr put out at the very beginning,
sentences.zh: 这就是比尔·巴尔在最开始发布的那四页信函，

sentences.en: stating that the special counsel had not found evidence of a criminal conspiracy or obstruction of justice.
sentences.zh: 声明特别检察官没有发现刑事共谋或妨碍司法的证据。

sentences.en: And what Bob Mueller was writing to say is your four pages did not adequately represent what our investigation found and that there appeared to be significant public confusion based on that four-page letter that you put out.
sentences.zh: 而鲍勃·穆勒写信是为了说，你的四页纸并没有充分代表我们调查的结果，而且基于你发布的那四页信函，公众似乎产生了严重的困惑。

sentences.en: And he makes an ask-a-bar that he put out executive summaries and introductions that were written by the special counsel's team and had been reviewed for redactions already and released those to the public so they can see more evidence right away.
sentences.zh: 他要求巴尔发布由特别检察官团队撰写的执行摘要和引言，这些内容已经过删减审查，并向公众发布，这样他们就能立即看到更多证据。

sentences.en: And why is this so significant, especially given the timing of when this letter becomes public?
sentences.zh: 为什么这如此重要，特别是考虑到这封信公开的时间点？

sentences.en: So, the letter just hours before senators are going to have to ask questions essentially confirms something that Democrats have been fearful of and suspicious of for weeks now,
sentences.zh: 所以，这封在参议员们不得不提问前几个小时公开的信，基本上证实了民主党人几周来一直担心和怀疑的事情，

sentences.en: which was there was a gulf between Bob Mueller and Bill Barr and that Bill Barr kind of stepped into the void, spoke for the Mueller investigation, and didn't do so fairly.
sentences.zh: 那就是鲍勃·穆勒和比尔·巴尔之间存在鸿沟，而比尔·巴尔某种程度上填补了这个空白，代表穆勒调查组发言，而且做得并不公正。

sentences.en: So, this is kind of a stunning thing for Robert Mueller, who we think of as this kind of mute legal figure to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于我们心目中那种沉默寡言的法律人物罗伯特·穆勒来说，这真是一件令人震惊的事情。

sentences.en: We have heard nothing publicly from Bob Mueller.
sentences.zh: 我们从未公开听到过鲍勃·穆勒的声音。

sentences.en: He has not spoken a word.
sentences.zh: 他一言未发。

sentences.en: He hasn't testified.
sentences.zh: 他没有作证。

sentences.en: He didn't give a press conference.
sentences.zh: 他没有举行新闻发布会。

sentences.en: And so, for him to write a letter to memorialize in writing to his boss, to Bill Barr, his dissatisfaction with his process, his concerns about it,
sentences.zh: 因此，他写信给他的上司比尔·巴尔，以书面形式记录下他对这一过程的不满和担忧，

sentences.en: underscores the significance of his concern and the stakes surrounding who's speaking for the investigation.
sentences.zh: 凸显了他担忧的重要性，以及谁来代表这项调查发言所带来的利害关系。

sentences.en: — Okay, so Nick, tell me about this hearing with Bill Barr once it actually gets started.
sentences.zh: ——好的，尼克，跟我说说比尔·巴尔的这场听证会，它一旦开始是什么样子的。

sentences.en: — So, Bill Barr stands, the cameras click, he puts up his right hand.
sentences.zh: ——比尔·巴尔站起来，相机快门声响起，他举起右手。

sentences.en: — You solemnly swear the testimony about the of this committee is the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but truth, except your God.
sentences.zh: ——你是否郑重宣誓，你向本委员会提供的证词是事实，全部的事实，除了事实别无其他，上帝保佑你。

sentences.en: — Yes.
sentences.zh: ——是的。

sentences.en: — And then he sits down.
sentences.zh: ——然后他坐下。

sentences.en: — Thank you, Mr. Chairman and Ranking Member Feinstein, members of the committee.
sentences.zh: ——谢谢主席先生、资深成员范斯坦，以及委员会的各位成员。

sentences.en: — In the same seat that just a few months ago,
sentences.zh: ——就在几个月前，他坐在同一个位置上，

sentences.en: he pledged to senators that he would let the Mueller investigation finish and that he would make its conclusions as public as he possibly could.
sentences.zh: 向参议员们承诺他会让穆勒调查完成，并会尽可能公开其结论。

sentences.en: — As you say, Bob Mueller was allowed to complete his work as he saw fit.
sentences.zh: ——正如你所说，鲍勃·穆勒被允许按照他认为合适的方式完成他的工作。

sentences.en: — And he said, look, I have done what I said I was going to do.
sentences.zh: ——他说，看，我已经做了我承诺要做的事情。

sentences.en: — I told this committee that I intended to exercise whatever discretion I had to make as much of the report available.
sentences.zh: ——我曾告诉本委员会，我打算行使我所拥有的任何酌情权，尽可能多地公开报告内容。

sentences.en: — And then he begins to shade into a kind of preemptive defense of himself.
sentences.zh: ——然后他开始转向一种对他自己的先发制人的辩护。

sentences.en: — I received a letter from Bob, the letter that's just been put into the record.
sentences.zh: ——我收到了鲍勃的一封信，这封信刚刚被记录在案。

sentences.en: — He says, essentially, I was surprised to receive this.
sentences.zh: ——他基本上说，收到这封信我很惊讶。

sentences.en: I got it out of the blue.
sentences.zh: 它是突然出现的。

sentences.en: I thought I was acting, and I think I did act in a transparent, timely way.
sentences.zh: 我以为我的行为是透明、及时的，而且我认为我确实做到了。

sentences.en: — I was not interested in putting out summaries.
sentences.zh: ——我没兴趣发布摘要。

sentences.en: And I wasn't going to put out the report piecemeal.
sentences.zh: 我也不打算零敲碎打地发布报告。

sentences.en: I wanted to get the whole report out.
sentences.zh: 我想把整份报告都发布出来。

sentences.en: — So basically, Barr is saying to these senators, I know you're about to ask me about this letter that Robert Mueller wrote to me.
sentences.zh: ——所以基本上，巴尔是在对这些参议员说，我知道你们正要问我关于罗伯特·穆勒写给我的这封信的事。

sentences.en: And I'm here to tell you that I had very good reasons to make the decisions I did.
sentences.zh: 我在这里告诉你们，我做出这些决定是有非常充分的理由的。

sentences.en: And Bob Mueller might be a great guy, but on this point, he's wrong.
sentences.zh: 鲍勃·穆勒可能是一个好人，但在这一点上，他错了。

sentences.en: — That's right.
sentences.zh: ——没错。

sentences.en: — So I'll end my statement there, Mr. Chairman, and glad to take any questions.
sentences.zh: ——那么我的陈述就到此为止，主席先生，很高兴回答任何问题。

sentences.en: — Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: ——非常感谢。

sentences.en: — And then it's the senator's turn.
sentences.zh: ——然后轮到参议员们了。

sentences.en: So what did they say?
sentences.zh: 他们说了什么？

sentences.en: — So they make clear very quickly that there are going to be two competing stories.
sentences.zh: ——他们很快明确表示，将会有两个相互竞争的故事。

sentences.en: — So what did we learn from this report?
sentences.zh: ——那么我们从这份报告中学到了什么？

sentences.en: — On the one side are the Republicans.
sentences.zh: ——一方面是共和党人。

sentences.en: — After all this time and all this money, Mr. Mueller and his team concluded there was no collusion.
sentences.zh: ——经过这么长时间和这么多钱，穆勒先生和他的团队得出结论，没有勾结。

sentences.en: — Who say there was no collusion.
sentences.zh: ——他们说没有勾结。

sentences.en: — As to obstruction of justice, Mr. Mueller left it to Mr. Barr to decide after two years.
sentences.zh: ——至于妨碍司法，穆勒先生在两年后将其留给巴尔先生决定。

sentences.en: And all this time, he said, Mr. Barr, you decide.
sentences.zh: 在这期间，他说，巴尔先生，由你来决定。

sentences.en: Mr. Barr did.
sentences.zh: 巴尔先生确实做了决定。

sentences.en: — There was no obstruction.
sentences.zh: ——没有妨碍司法。

sentences.en: — I appreciate very much what Mr. Mueller did for the country.
sentences.zh: ——我非常感谢穆勒先生为这个国家所做的一切。

sentences.en: — I have read most of the report.
sentences.zh: ——我已经读了大部分报告。

sentences.en: — This investigation—
sentences.zh: ——这项调查——

sentences.en: — It is over.
sentences.zh: ——已经结束了。

sentences.en: — Is over.
sentences.zh: ——已经结束了。

sentences.en: — Senator Feinstein.
sentences.zh: ——范斯坦参议员。

sentences.en: — The Democrats have a very different story.
sentences.zh: ——民主党人有完全不同的说法。

sentences.en: — Contrary to the declarations of the total and complete exoneration, the special counsel's report contained substantial evidence of misconduct.
sentences.zh: ——与所谓彻底完全开脱的声明相反，特别检察官的报告包含了大量不当行为的证据。

sentences.en: — They believe that Mr. Barr has been acting as a partisan actor, and they were out to prove it.
sentences.zh: ——他们认为巴尔先生一直表现得像个党派参与者，他们要证明这一点。

sentences.en: — You concluded, and I quote, that the evidence is not sufficient to establish that the president committed an obstruction of justice offense, end quote.
sentences.zh: ——你得出的结论是，我引用一下，证据不足以确定总统犯有妨碍司法罪，引用结束。

sentences.en: — However, special counsel Mueller methodically outlines 10 episodes, some continuing multiple actions by the president to mislead the American people.
sentences.zh: ——然而，特别检察官穆勒有条不紊地列出了10个情节，其中一些包含总统误导美国人民的多项行为。

sentences.en: — And they try and build a case that this investigation cannot end.
sentences.zh: ——他们试图建立一个论点，即这项调查不能结束。

sentences.en: — Congress has both the constitutional duty and the authority to investigate the serious findings contained in the Mueller report.
sentences.zh: ——国会有宪法赋予的职责和权力去调查穆勒报告中包含的严重发现。

sentences.en: — That the rule of law is at stake, that big ideas like the separation of powers and the accountability of the presidency hang in the balance.
sentences.zh: ——法治正处于危险之中，权力分立和总统问责制等重大理念正悬而未决。

sentences.en: — And that to stop an investigation now would be an abdication of Congress's authority.
sentences.zh: ——现在停止调查将是国会权力的放弃。

sentences.en: — Thank you, Mr. Chairman.
sentences.zh: ——谢谢主席先生。

sentences.en: — Well, so how exactly are these two sides on this committee making their cases here?
sentences.zh: ——那么，委员会里的这两派人究竟是如何在这里陈述他们的观点的呢？

sentences.en: — Let's start with the Republicans.
sentences.zh: ——让我们从共和党人开始。

sentences.en: — So Republican senator after Republican senator seemed to zoom, in most cases, first directly towards the fact that,
sentences.zh: ——所以，共和党参议员们似乎一个接一个地，在大多数情况下，直接指向一个事实，即：

sentences.en: as Barr made very clear and as he decided in the case of obstruction, the president did not break a law.
sentences.zh: 正如巴尔明确指出的，以及他在妨碍司法案件中所裁定的那样，总统没有触犯法律。

sentences.en: — Very quickly, give us your reasoning why you think it would be inappropriate to proceed forward on obstruction of justice in this case.
sentences.zh: ——请快速告诉我们，为什么你认为在本案中继续推进妨碍司法调查是不合适的？

sentences.en: — Well, generally speaking, an obstruction case typically has two aspects to it.
sentences.zh: ——嗯，总的来说，妨碍司法案件通常有两个方面。

sentences.en: One, there's usually an underlying criminality that's being—
sentences.zh: 第一，通常存在一个潜在的犯罪行为，正在——

sentences.en: — Let's stop right there.
sentences.zh: ——让我们停在那儿。

sentences.en: — Yeah.
sentences.zh: ——是的。

sentences.en: — Was there an underlying crime here?
sentences.zh: ——这里有潜在的犯罪行为吗？

sentences.en: — No.
sentences.zh: ——没有。

sentences.en: — Many of them, at the same time, asked Mr. Barr about questions that have been a hobby horse of the president and of certain Republicans for quite a while now, which is,
sentences.zh: ——他们中的许多人同时问巴尔先生一些问题，这些问题一直是总统和某些共和党人相当长一段时间以来的心头好，那就是：

sentences.en: what about these allegations that there were spying on the campaign?
sentences.zh: 关于竞选活动受到监视的指控是怎么回事？

sentences.en: — Have you already tasked any staff to look into whether spying by the FBI and other agencies on the Trump campaign was properly predicated?
sentences.zh: ——你是否已经指派任何工作人员去调查联邦调查局和其他机构对特朗普竞选活动的监视是否具有正当理由？

sentences.en: And can Congress expect a formal report on your findings?
sentences.zh: 国会能期待一份关于你调查结果的正式报告吗？

sentences.en: — Yes, I do have people in the department helping me review the activities over the summer of 2016.
sentences.zh: ——是的，我确实有部门里的人在帮我审查2016年夏季的活动。

sentences.en: — What about these incredibly biased text messages that two of the lead FBI officials working on this were exchanging with each other?
sentences.zh: ——那么，参与此案的两名主要联邦调查局官员之间交换的那些极其偏见的短信是怎么回事？

sentences.en: — This is a text message from Peter Strzok,
sentences.zh: ——这是一条来自彼得·斯特佐克的短信，

sentences.en: a top counterintelligence investigator who we now know helped launch this counter-spy investigation of the president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 他是一位高级反间谍调查员，我们现在知道他帮助发起了针对美国总统的这项反间谍调查。

sentences.en: Peter Strzok says, just went to a Southern Virginia Walmart.
sentences.zh: 彼得·斯特佐克说，刚去了南弗吉尼亚的一家沃尔玛。

sentences.en: I could smell the Trump support.
sentences.zh: 我能闻到特朗普支持者的味道。

sentences.en: Smell is capitalized.
sentences.zh: “味道”这个词是大写的。

sentences.en: — How are we supposed to believe that this was a fair investigation, especially when, at the end of the day, it didn't prove any wrongdoing?
sentences.zh: ——我们怎么能相信这是一次公平的调查，尤其是当最终它没有证明任何不当行为时？

sentences.en: — There were two investigations here.
sentences.zh: ——这里有两项调查。

sentences.en: One was an investigation of Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 一项是对唐纳德·特朗普的调查。

sentences.en: There was another investigation of Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 另一项是对希拉里·克林顿的调查。

sentences.en: — And then they return to another familiar Republican target.
sentences.zh: ——然后他们又回到了另一个熟悉的共和党目标。

sentences.en: They say President Trump may have been treated with political bias, but so was the case of Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 他们说特朗普总统可能受到了政治偏见的对待，但希拉里·克林顿的案件也是如此。

sentences.en: She was gone easy on by many of these same FBI officials.
sentences.zh: 许多同样的联邦调查局官员对她却网开一面。

sentences.en: — These are the people that made a decision that Clinton didn't do anything wrong, and a counterintelligence investigation of the Trump campaign was warranted.
sentences.zh: ——这些人做出了克林顿没有做错任何事的决定，却认为对特朗普竞选团队进行反间谍调查是合理的。

sentences.en: We're going to, in a bipartisan way, I hope, deal with Russia.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们能以两党合作的方式处理俄罗斯问题。

sentences.en: But when the Mueller report is put to bed, and it soon will be, this committee is going to look long and hard in how this all started.
sentences.zh: 但当穆勒报告尘埃落定，且很快就会如此时，本委员会将深入仔细地审视这一切是如何开始的。

sentences.en: — So this is the Republicans making the case for basically investigating the investigators, the FBI, the apparatus that brought the Russia investigation as far as it did.
sentences.zh: 所以，共和党人现在是在主张调查那些调查者，也就是FBI，以及那个将“通俄门”调查推进到这一步的机构。

sentences.en: Because in their minds, since there are no charges, this was a kind of a smear campaign,
sentences.zh: 因为在他们看来，既然没有提出指控，这就是一场抹黑运动，

sentences.en: and the focus of any investigative apparatus now should be understanding how it got this far.
sentences.zh: 而现在任何调查机构的重点都应该是弄清楚事情是怎么发展到这一步的。

sentences.en: — That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And we've seen the president and some of his most conservative allies for more than a year now make this argument.
sentences.zh: 一年多来，我们一直看到总统和他的一些最保守的盟友在提出这种论点。

sentences.en: But what we saw today, I think, was the full Republican Party embracing that idea,
sentences.zh: 但我认为，我们今天所看到的是整个共和党都在拥护这一观点，

sentences.en: that the moment has finally come where what Trump has been clamoring for is actually going to come to pass.
sentences.zh: 即特朗普一直呼吁的事情终于要实现了。

sentences.en: — Have you looked into the decision by the FBI into why they launched a counterintelligence investigation?
sentences.zh: 你有没有调查过FBI发起反间谍调查的决定原因？

sentences.en: — I am looking into it, and I have looked into it.
sentences.zh: 我正在调查，而且我已经调查过了。

sentences.en: — And you will—will you commit to telling us what you find as the result of your own review and investigation?
sentences.zh: 那么你是否承诺，会将你审查和调查的结果告诉我们？

sentences.en: — Well, at the end of the day, when I form conclusions, I intend to share it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，归根结底，当我得出结论时，我打算分享它。

sentences.en: — I'll take that as a yes.
sentences.zh: 我就当你是答应了。让我问你——

sentences.en: Let me ask you—
sentences.zh: 好的，那是共和党人的立场。

sentences.en: — OK, so that's the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 司法委员会的民主党人呢？

sentences.en: What about the Democrats on the Judiciary Committee?
sentences.zh: 他们在这里是如何陈述自己的观点的？

sentences.en: How are they making their case here?
sentences.zh: 首先，他们从质询比尔·巴尔关于他和鲍勃·穆勒之间那封新信件的内容开始。

sentences.en: — First and foremost, they start by interrogating Bill Barr about this new letter between he and Bob Mueller.
sentences.zh: 穆勒先生写道，你的信威胁到了司法部任命特别检察官的核心目的。

sentences.en: — Mr. Mueller wrote that your letter threatened to undermine a central purpose for which the department appointed the special counsel.
sentences.zh: 即确保公众对调查结果的充分信任。

sentences.en: To assure full public confidence in the outcome of the investigation.
sentences.zh: 他们想知道为什么比尔·巴尔几周前告诉另一个国会委员会，

sentences.en: — They're interested in why Bill Barr told another congressional committee a couple of weeks ago
sentences.zh: 说他不知道为什么穆勒或他的调查人员会对他在报告中的表述方式感到不满。

sentences.en: that he didn't know why Mueller or his investigators may be dissatisfied with the way he had talked about the report.
sentences.zh: 我对你在这里以及在另一个机构的证词感到有些困扰。

sentences.en: — I'm somewhat troubled by your testimony here and in the other body.
sentences.zh: 你曾于4月9日在众议院作证。

sentences.en: You appeared before the House of Corporations on April 9th.
sentences.zh: 在穆勒团队传出不满的媒体报道后，他在众议院听证会上被问到，你知道这是怎么回事吗？

sentences.en: — He was asked in a House hearing after there were press reports of dissatisfaction on the Mueller team, you know, what's up with that?
sentences.zh: 你知道这背后的原因吗？

sentences.en: Do you know what's behind this?
sentences.zh: 当国会议员，我想是克里斯议员，

sentences.en: — When the congressman, I believe it was Congressman Chris,
sentences.zh: 问你是否知道特别检察官团队成员担心的是什么时。

sentences.en: asked if you knew what those members of the special counsel's team were concerned about.
sentences.zh: 你回答说，不，我不知道。

sentences.en: You testified in response, no, I don't.
sentences.zh: 他给出的回答含糊其辞，但意思就是不知道。

sentences.en: — And he basically gave a little bit of a squishy answer, but the effect of it was no.
sentences.zh: 所以参议员们想知道。

sentences.en: And so senators wanted to know.
sentences.zh: 为什么你在4月9日作证说你不知道穆勒团队表达的担忧，

sentences.en: — Why did you testify on April 9th that you didn't know the concerns being expressed by Mueller's team,
sentences.zh: 而事实上你两周前就直接从穆勒先生那里听到了这些担忧？

sentences.en: when in fact you had heard those concerns directly from Mr. Mueller two weeks before?
sentences.zh: 你当时手里拿着这封信。

sentences.en: — You had this letter in your hand at this point.
sentences.zh: 你在说什么呢？

sentences.en: What were you talking about?
sentences.zh: 你知道穆勒的问题所在。

sentences.en: You knew what Mueller's problem was.
sentences.zh: 他当时手里拿着穆勒那封明确写着“我不满意你总结事情的方式”的信，

sentences.en: — He had the Mueller letter that explicitly said,
sentences.zh: 却在另一个委员会面前说，我不太明白你在说什么。

sentences.en: I'm not happy with how you summarize things, at the moment that he went before this other committee and said, I don't quite know what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: — That's right.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，他还作证说，事实上他一收到信，就拿起电话打给穆勒说，

sentences.en: And not only that, he testified that in fact he, as soon as he got the letter, picked up the phone and called Mueller and said,
sentences.zh: 鲍勃，这封信是怎么回事？

sentences.en: — Bob, what's with the letter?
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 如果有问题，直接打电话给我。

sentences.en: let the phone and call me if there's an issue.
sentences.zh: 巴尔似乎一直在向民主党人淡化这段时间差和理解偏差的重要性。

sentences.en: — And consistently Barr seemed to downplay to Democrats what the significance of this lapse of time and understanding was.
sentences.zh: 我直接和鲍勃谈过，鲍勃告诉我他对准确性没有异议。

sentences.en: — I talked directly to Bob, and Bob told me that he did not have objections to the accuracy.
sentences.zh: 他本质上是说，这只是个无聊的争论。

sentences.en: — He essentially said, you know, this is a silly dispute.
sentences.zh: 如果我最终像我所做的那样发布了完整报告，那又有什么区别呢？

sentences.en: If I end up putting out the full report as I did, what difference does it make?
sentences.zh: 公众现在可以去查看它了。

sentences.en: The public can now go and view it.
sentences.zh: 他们现在可以做出自己的判断了。

sentences.en: They can now make their own judgments.
sentences.zh: 在长达数月的审判后，如果我想在完整记录准备好之前向公众公布裁决，

sentences.en: — After a, you know, months-long trial, if I wanted to go out and get out to the public what the verdict was, pending preparation of the full transcript, and I'm out there saying,
sentences.zh: 我站在外面说，这就是裁决，然后检察官走过来拍拍我的肩膀说，嗯，这个裁决并没有完全涵盖我所有的工作。

sentences.en: here's the verdict, and the prosecutor comes up and taps me on the shoulder and says, well, the verdict doesn't really fully capture all my work.
sentences.zh: 我做的那些精彩的交叉询问怎么样？

sentences.en: How about that great, you know, cross-examination I did?
sentences.zh: 或者我在审判第三天做的那件事怎么样？

sentences.en: Or how about that third day of trial where I did that?
sentences.zh: 这并没有涵盖一切。

sentences.en: This doesn't capture everything.
sentences.zh: 我的回答是，我并不是要涵盖一切。

sentences.en: My answer to that is I'm not trying to capture everything.
sentences.zh: 我只是想陈述裁决结果。

sentences.en: I'm just trying to state the verdict.
sentences.zh: 令我印象深刻的是，巴尔借此机会说，记住。

sentences.en: — I was struck by the fact that Barr took his opportunity to basically say, remember.
sentences.zh: 决定如何以及何时公开报告的是我，而不是鲍勃·穆勒。

sentences.en: — And it was my decision how and when to make it public, not Bob Mueller's.
sentences.zh: 我是这里的老板。

sentences.en: — I'm the boss here.
sentences.zh: 当涉及到披露什么内容时，那是我的决定，而不是罗伯特·穆勒的。

sentences.en: When it comes to what gets disclosed, that's my decision, not Robert Mueller's.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: — That's right.
sentences.zh: 这就是巴尔回归到他作为司法部长的权威以及管理特别检察官的具体法规的地方。

sentences.en: This is where Barr fell back both on his authority as attorney general and the specific regulation governing the special counsel.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是说，穆勒把这个“孩子”交给我后，我就拥有了控制权。

sentences.en: And he said, basically, I have control of the baby after Mueller handed it over to me.
sentences.zh: 如果鲍勃不满意，我深表遗憾。

sentences.en: And I'm sorry if Bob was dissatisfied, essentially.
sentences.zh: 他是我的雇员。

sentences.en: — He's my employee.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是鲍勃的老板。

sentences.en: — Yeah, I'm Bob's boss.
sentences.zh: 特别检察官的报告描述了总统如何指示白宫法律顾问唐·麦克加恩解雇特别检察官穆勒，

sentences.en: — The special counsel's report describes how the president directed White House counsel Don
sentences.zh: 后来又告诉麦克加恩写一封信，引用“为了我们的记录”，说明总统并没有命令他解雇穆勒。

sentences.en: McGahn to fire special counsel Mueller and later told McGahn to write a letter, quote, for our records, end quote, stating that the president had not ordered him to fire Mueller.
sentences.zh: 然后，委员会中级别最高的民主党人黛安·范斯坦，开始梳理

sentences.en: — And then Dianne Feinstein, who's the top Democrat on the committee, basically starts walking through
sentences.zh: 总统与他的白宫法律顾问唐·麦克加恩之间的互动证据，麦克加恩是穆勒调查的重要证人。

sentences.en: the evidence around the president's interactions with Don McGahn, his White House counsel, who was an important witness for the Mueller investigation.
sentences.zh: 报告还叙述了总统如何多次试图让麦克加恩改变他的说法。

sentences.en: — The report also recounts how the president made repeated efforts to get McGahn to change his story.
sentences.zh: 她正在向司法部长施压，要求他看看这种行为。

sentences.en: — And is pressing the attorney general to say, look at this behavior.
sentences.zh: 现行法律是否禁止试图让证人撒谎，说出证人认为虚假的事情？

sentences.en: — Does existing law prohibit efforts to get a witness to lie to say something the witness believes is false?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: — Yes.
sentences.zh: 向政府撒谎，是的。

sentences.en: Lie to the government, yes.
sentences.zh: 看看总统告诉麦克加恩解雇特别检察官，因为他有利益冲突。

sentences.en: — Look at the president telling McGahn to get rid of the special counsel because he has conflicts.
sentences.zh: 这怎么不是妨碍司法公正？

sentences.en: How is that not obstruction of justice?
sentences.zh: 这怎么不符合你的标准？

sentences.en: How does that not meet your criteria?
sentences.zh: 你仍然面临这样一种情况，即总统试图改变

sentences.en: — You still have a situation where a president essentially tries to change
sentences.zh: 律师的陈述，以防止对自己进行进一步的批评。

sentences.en: the lawyer's account in order to prevent further criticism of himself.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那不是犯罪。

sentences.en: — Well, that's not a crime.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这种情况下，你可以指示某人撒谎？

sentences.en: — So you can, in this situation, instruct someone to lie?
sentences.zh: 不，必须是——嗯，要构成妨碍司法公正，谎言必须与损害特定程序中的证据有关。

sentences.en: — No, it has to be—well, to be obstruction of justice, the lie has to be tied to impairing the evidence in a particular proceeding.
sentences.zh: 他们开始梳理穆勒报告中列出的10个实例，

sentences.en: — And they begin to work through what are basically
sentences.zh: 并带着怀疑的态度听着巴尔的回应，

sentences.en: 10 instances that the Mueller report lays out and kind of incredulously listen as Barr comes back
sentences.zh: 这些回应在法律上非常精确，有时又非常琐碎，我认为对民主党人来说，

sentences.en: with very legally precise and sometimes quite in the weeds kind of answers that I think for Democrats
sentences.zh: 这些话听起来很空洞，但却让巴尔能够继续在这些问题中周旋。

sentences.en: ring hollow but allow Barr to keep maneuvering forward through these questions.
sentences.zh: 那么，尼克，通过这些交流和证词，我们对比尔·巴尔有了什么了解？

sentences.en: — So, Nick, what are we learning about Bill Barr through these exchanges and through this testimony?
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是一位对自己的法律理解和判断力充满自信的司法部长，

sentences.en: — So what we see is an attorney general who is supremely confident in his understanding of the law,
sentences.zh: 而且他对总统的行政权力有着宽泛的看法。

sentences.en: in his own judgments, and has a generous view of the president's executive power.
sentences.zh: 这些是我们早就知道关于比尔·巴尔的事实，在很大程度上，他正如共和党人和民主党人似乎预料的那样表现出来。

sentences.en: — These are things that we knew were true about Bill Barr, and to a remarkable degree, he is acting them out just as Republicans and Democrats seem to agree that he would.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他今天不是一个乐观的证人，但他也没有被那些在某些情况下当面要求他辞职的民主党人所激怒。

sentences.en: I mean, he was not an upbeat witness today, but he also wasn't ruffled by Democrats who, in some cases, were calling for him to his face to resign.
sentences.zh: 你辜负了这份信任。美国值得更好的。你应该辞职。

sentences.en: — You have betrayed that truSt. America deserves better.
sentences.zh: 我们称他为尴尬，并将他与总统一些最坚定的政治捍卫者相提并论，而他只是默默地继续前进。

sentences.en: You should resign.
sentences.zh: 他没有被拉去批评总统，也没有在自己的行为上退让半分。

sentences.en: — We're calling him an embarrassment and comparing him to some of the president's staunchest political defenders, and he just trudged forward.
sentences.zh: 你实际上是为总统开脱或洗清了罪名。

sentences.en: He was not pulled into criticizing the president, nor was he—did he give an inch on his own behavior.
sentences.zh: 不，我没有开脱。

sentences.en: — You, in effect, exonerated or cleared the president.
sentences.zh: 我说的是我们认为没有足够的证据来确定妨碍司法罪，这是司法部的工作。

sentences.en: — No, I didn't exonerate.
sentences.zh: 感觉如果比尔·巴尔在批评谁或什么事——这对我来说有点惊讶，因为我觉得他们长期以来一直是朋友——他是在

sentences.en: I said that we did not believe that there was sufficient evidence to establish an obstruction offense, which is the job of the Justice Department.
sentences.zh: 批评特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒及其办公室。

sentences.en: — It felt like if Bill Barr was criticizing anybody or anything—and this was a bit of a surprise for me, because my sense is that they have been friends for a long time—he was
sentences.zh: 这是他今天证词中比较引人注目的方面之一。

sentences.en: criticizing the special counsel, Robert Mueller, and his office.
sentences.zh: 他一次又一次地提到他的老朋友鲍勃·穆勒，并基本上把一些责任归咎于他。

sentences.en: — This was one of the more remarkable aspects of his testimony today.
sentences.zh: 你是否同意他在报告第二卷中提出的不做出决定的理由，为什么同意或不同意？

sentences.en: Time and again, he brought up his old friend, Bob Mueller, and essentially cast some, you know, blame onto him.
sentences.zh: 我不太确定他的推理。

sentences.en: — Do you agree with the reasons that he offered for not making a decision in volume two of his

sentences.en: report, and why or why not?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这封信有点刻薄，我认为这可能是他的某位工作人员写的。

sentences.en: — I'm not really sure of his reasoning.
sentences.zh: “蔑视”这个词可能太强烈了，但这并不是我们习惯听到的谈论鲍勃·穆勒的那种敬意或关系，

sentences.en: — And then, very near the end of the hearing, after the senators had gone around and around on this letter, he described it as,
sentences.zh: 我们可能期望司法部长对一位他合作如此密切的特别检察官表现出这种态度。

sentences.en: — You know, the letter's a bit snitty, and I think it was probably written by one of his staff people.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
